minutes.headline: Select Board renewed all 2025 licenses, voted a skate park grant letter, and tabled the tax-foreclosure hold-or-sell decision.
minutes.summary: The board renewed alcohol, auto dealer, common victualer and limousine licenses, approved a T-Mobile grant support letter for the skate park, and voted to vacate a foreclosure judgment on a Sunset Avenue property upon full redemption. It heard the interim town manager report, an ARPA spending update, and discussed climate survey and goal-setting policies. A decision to retain or sell two foreclosed parcels under the new state law was held to next week.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the board and PACTV, wished two 101-year-old veterans happy birthday, announced Santa at Town Center Saturday and Salvation Army bell ringing by the chiefs.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to approve its skate park letter of support, with modifications noted.
The board voted unanimously to vacate a tax-lien foreclosure judgment on one Sunset Avenue property, subject to full redemption payment within 14 days.
The board put off deciding whether to retain or sell two foreclosed parcels under the new state law until next week, pending property cards and photos.
The board renewed the 2025 alcohol, auto dealer, common victualer and limousine licenses, each by unanimous vote.
The finance director's year-end report was postponed to next week, and a vote on the remaining ARPA contingency was deferred.

why_it_matters: Whether the town keeps or sells foreclosed parcels under the new state law decides if they return to private hands and the tax rolls or stay town property, and that vote is still ahead.
The ARPA contingency vote and the finance director's year-end report were both pushed back, so residents have not yet seen the closing figures or the use of the remaining federal funds.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting: the retain-or-sell decision on 531 Reservoir Road and 56 Carr Avenue, the remaining ARPA contingency vote, and the finance director's year-end report.
An ARPA spending report to be published, likely in January.
